text: A small company in a shared, indifferent sky.

Everything under this sky is shared. The air, the ducts, the hulls that creak like something asleep, and every credit anyone earns, which goes into the Common Ledger and comes back in portions. The Plan is generous. The Plan is also five cycles long, and then another five.

There is one form for leaving: a Release. It takes you off the ledger and sells you a planet nobody has counted. It is sold in credits, to fellow hands who have them.

So you have a small company, one ship's worth of cash, three planets and two goods. Buy where it is cheap. Sell where it is not. Serving the common good is encouraged. Profit, officially, is a typing error.

The sky will not notice either way.

text: Skills cost skill points, never credits.

You did it the plain way: buy, sell, repeat. The Release came through stamped, and the Bureau did not look up. The planet is yours, uncounted and quiet. The Commons will list you as a clerical error. You can live with that. The door is open. Walk through it.

The Plan was almost closed. In the final cycle the numbers lined up and the goal was met with nothing to spare. The clerk stamped your Release as the lights in the office went down for the night. You earned the planet, and the memory of every cycle you spent counting. Standing on it now you feel more relief than joy, then a little more joy than you expected. Some things only count when they nearly do not.

You knew each price before it moved and each event before it arrived. The goal fell to you like a sum on a page, and the Release was a formality. The planet is yours, exact and silent. You look at the horizon and see a column of figures. It balances. It always balances. The Bureau has sent a kind letter, offering you a desk. You are not sure when you stopped being the one who escaped, and became the one who counts.

You reached further than the rest, and it paid. Every permit, every beacon and every distant pair of planets added to the map until the map had a gap in it, and the gap was yours. The Release is filed. The planet sits at the edge of what anyone has charted, beyond the reach of any form. Behind you the company hums on without you, and the Plan does not know your name. Ahead, nothing at all, which is exactly what you came for.

You built a company that holds. Well-kept hulls, deep holds, goods moving on time. The cash goal came the way tides do. The Release came with a note: the Commons thanks you for your service and asks that the supply line stay open. You put down a small dock, a bench and a light on your own ground. A ship arrives every few days with exactly what you ordered. It is escape, mostly. You have never been anywhere you were so little in a hurry to leave.

You learned a little of everything and bet on nothing in particular. The goal came anyway, and with it the Release, and a planet no ledger has yet counted. Standing on it you notice the question the whole voyage was built to postpone: what is the amount that is enough? You have it now. You are not sure it was the amount you named at the start. The Commons would say enough is shared. The sky has no opinion. You sit down, and for a while decide not to count.
Goal reached in cycle {cycle} with {cash} credits.

text: You built the lines first, and everything else stood on them. Deep holds at Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate, hulls that ran to time, and then the same pattern in every system on the chart. The goal came the way tides do. The Release was filed in order, and the Bureau, polite to the end, asked only that the supply stay open. You said it would. You put down a dock on your own ground, a bench and a light. A ship came in that evening with exactly what you had ordered, and the hold hummed like something asleep. Along the way you learned which shelf fills first at Tillam, which hull sulks at Ashgate, and how long Voltara can run on a full hold. None of it is written in any ledger. All of it is why the thing works. You have escaped. It is strange to be so well supplied by the thing you left.
Every few days a ship arrives on time. You have stopped minding.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You read the sky the way others read a form. Prices at Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate, and then at every market beyond, were known to you before they moved. The goal fell the way a sum falls. The Release was filed and returned by morning, stamped, and the planet is yours. Nothing there surprises you. You check the forecast from habit, and the habit finds nothing to forecast. You remember the first cycles, when a price rise was news and not arithmetic. You miss them a little. Nobody warned you that certainty is also a kind of quiet, and that the quiet has a hum of its own. That is the cost of knowing: the horizon arrives already counted. The Bureau's letter, offering you a desk, lies unopened on the table. You have not decided what that says about you.
The letter stays unopened. The figures keep adding up anyway.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: Every permit, every beacon, every distant pair of planets: you charted them all, and the map ended where you wanted it to. The Release was filed from the last system anyone has a name for. The planet you bought lies beyond it, a pale rock under a patient sun, uncounted by any ledger. Behind you the company runs on, and the Plan does not know your name. Ahead there is one ridge. You put a light on it yourself. You remember Voltara as a small bright place with a loud reactor, and Tillam and Ashgate as the first two names you learned. They look very close from here, like pins on a table. You came a long way to be this alone, and you are exactly as alone as you hoped.
Out here the sky is wider than the Plan. You leave the light on anyway.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You learned more than one trade and kept every one. The lines ran, the forecasts held, the map grew past Ashgate and past the last beacon. The goal came when you were ready for it. The Release was filed without a single correction, which the clerk remarked on, politely, as unusual. The planet is yours, uncounted, with a dock, a window and a long view. Nothing in the company is a mystery to you. You could name every hold at Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate from memory, and every beacon after them. This is rarer than it sounds, and you earned it one cycle at a time. You know what enough is now, and it is not the amount you named at the start. You sit down. The sky has no opinion. For once you are glad of it.
You count nothing tonight. The Commons will have to manage without you.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You stayed. The company stays on the Common Ledger, and the work goes on as before: buy, sell, repeat. The Bureau thanks you for your continued contribution. Nothing changes much, and that is the whole ending. The ships still run. The numbers still move. It is a living.

You stayed, and the company became part of how the Commons eats. Your holds keep the shelves full and your ships keep the dock times. The Bureau enters you in the Common Ledger as a service, with a small line of thanks. Nobody forgets what you carry, and nobody thanks you twice. The goal is behind you. The work is still in front. It is a quiet kind of power. You are needed, which is a way of belonging the forms do not mention.

You stayed, and the company became what the Commons feared and, in quiet hours, consulted. You knew the prices before the Bureau did. Now the Bureau asks. A committee sits, a polite clerk takes notes, and your forecast becomes the Plan's. You are not in charge. You are only never wrong, which in a society that shares everything is the more awkward thing to be. The Common Ledger gives you a column of your own. It is the longest column.

You stayed, and the company kept growing. Permits, beacons and far routes made a map that now includes you. The Bureau drafts a new form to describe what you have become, and then a second form, because the first did not fit. You are a corporation: a small Commons of your own, with ships, holds and a long view. The sky is as large as it was. You have only built a bigger door into it.

You stayed, and the company carries on as a bit of everything: some lines, some forecasts, some reach. The Bureau enters it in the Common Ledger as a going concern, which sounds like a compliment and is a classification. The ships run. The accounts balance. The Commons neither fears you nor needs you very much, and that is its own sort of freedom. Tomorrow there is a cycle, and then another.

You stayed, and the company grew into the thing the Commons lives on. Holds at Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate and in every system after them, ships on time, shelves full. When a harvest failed or a reactor sulked, your stock covered it, and no one wrote that down. The Bureau gave you a seat on the supply committee, and you arrived early. Nobody calls you a corporation now. They call you the line. Once, at Tillam, a clerk asked what you were for. You said you were not sure. The clerk wrote it down as an answer. You did not escape, and you were not absorbed. You are load-bearing. In the dark the holds hum, and the lights stay on in a great many kitchens.
A great many kitchens are warm tonight. None of them know your name. That is the job.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You stayed, and the company became the thing the Commons feared: a firm that is never surprised. You read Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate, and then every market beyond, and the forecasts came true so often that the Bureau stopped checking them. The next Plan was drafted from your figures. The one after was drafted by you, with the clerks taking notes. Voltara's reactors are scheduled by your numbers. Ashgate's harvests are sold by your numbers. Tillam's committee has stopped meeting on the days you are quiet. Nobody was forced. It was simply easier to ask. The Common Ledger lists the company as a corporation and the Plan as its client. In the cold the screens glow, and the numbers behind them are yours.
The next five-cycle plan arrives with your figures in it. No one remembers asking.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You stayed, and the company walked outward until it had a sky of its own. Permits in every system, beacons on every ridge, routes across distances the Plan only drew in pencil. The Bureau has a form for a company this large. It is called a Commons. You are not quite one and not quite the other, and a few systems now call you when something breaks. At the far edge of the chart a light burns that you did not install. The ships you started with are the smallest thing on the books now. You keep one Skerrit in a bay, out of habit, with the lamp on. You did not build an escape. You built somewhere to escape to, with a ledger of your own.
At the far edge of the chart, someone files a form with your name at the top.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: You stayed, and the company is all of it: the holds, the forecasts, the reach. The lines run through Voltara, Tillam and Ashgate and out into every system on the chart. The Bureau is unsure whether to fear you or thank you, and has settled on a form that does both. You are the thing the Commons feared and the thing it quietly needs, and the two turn out to be one company. You began with a few hulls and an empty ledger on Voltara. Tillam and Ashgate were the whole world then. Now they are the first two lines on a very long page, and you know the page by heart. The ships come and go. The ledger is long. Outside the glass the hull creaks, as if turning over in its sleep, and goes on.
The Commons runs on you, and fears you, and files both under thanks.
place: End screen, after the ending text

text: The Plan closed before the goal was met. The Release was never filed. The Bureau is very kind about it. Your company is entered in the Common Ledger, your ships assigned to the common good, and your name given a quota that is fair and equal and exactly the size of everyone else's. No one is cruel. The sky is as large as it was, and it did not notice. A different company, a different run, might read the prices sooner. Count what you have. It is more than you started with, and less than you needed.

A cloud of broken hull and spent tanks has settled into orbit over {planet}. A contractor offers to clear it for a fee. The Bureau has filed the debris as "unowned", which is how it stayed.

Engineers propose a partial shield over the sun. Residents dislike it. It would change the resource mix on planets you can buy later: some resources fall, and you earn more profit and energy there. Planets you already own are not affected.
Planets you can buy later change: some resources drop, profit and energy rise.
Nothing changes. The sun keeps its full light.

The shield is in place. Residents are unhappy and say so, in writing. On planets you can buy later, some resources fall, and profit and energy rise. Planets you own are unchanged. The sky is a little dimmer.
The plans go back into the cabinet. Residents are relieved and file no thanks. Nothing changes in any market.
Nomad families live on the asteroids you could mine. They have no entry on the Common Ledger, which the Bureau regards as a personal failing. You can evict them and mine the rock, or let them stay.
The asteroids open for mining. Some nomads turn to piracy, and pirates rise.
The asteroids stay closed to mining. No pirates come of it.
The nomads left on the next tide, quietly. The rock is yours to mine. Some of them did not go far, and they now keep ships and a grudge. Pirates rise.
You let the nomads stay. Their lamps burn on the rock, small and steady. The asteroids remain closed to mining.
Pirates now work the lanes, and fewer cargoes get through. Trade volume falls while they stay. The Bureau has opened a file on them. It is a thin file.
Pay to have the pirates cleared. It costs credits and removes their effect on trade.

The Bureau reports an asteroid on a slow path toward the system. The state can deflect it for a payment. The form for refusing is shorter than the form for paying. The dark outside has begun to look closer.
Cost: payment to the state. Asteroid dealt with. The company gains one expansion point.
An even chance: company storage is hit, or nothing happens.
The state turned the rock aside and sent a receipt. The company gains one expansion point for the trouble. The asteroid drifts on, toward someone else's sky.
Event reward: the asteroid is dealt with and the company gains an expansion point.
The asteroid struck {planet}. Your company storage there is gone, and what it held with it. The Bureau has recorded the loss as an adjustment of the Common Ledger.
The asteroid grazed {planet}. Your company storage there is cracked and holds less than before. The Bureau has recorded the damage as "partial".
The asteroid passed the system and kept going. Nothing was hit and nothing changes. The Bureau has withdrawn its warning, with regret.
